newsitem.title: FINLAND: Fair Helsinki ends off on nerves ahead U.S. jobs.
newsitem.headline: Fair Helsinki ends off on nerves ahead U.S. jobs.

text.p: Finnish shares fell in fair volume on Thursday with the decline in Nokia only partly offset by year-high prices for Outokumpu and Hartwall after their stronger-than-forecast January-April earnings, brokers said.
The sentiment was subdued by Nokia's fall after its overnight slide on Wall Street, and by nervousness ahead of the release of U.S. May payrolls and unemployment data on Friday.

"Many big institutional investors have been clearly on the sidelines today due to jitters ahead of Friday's data," one broker said. Nokia recovered some early losses to end 5.50 markka or 1.6 percent down at 339.40 markka.

Favourable metal market trends and the stronger dollar boosted Outokumpu's four-month earnings and brokers saw further upside for the share, particularly due to the brighter outlook for zinc prices. Outokumpu was up nearly the whole session but eded unchanged at 103 markka after hitting a year-high 106.50.

The bourse was expected to be hesitant on Friday amid more domestic earnings reports (including Tamro, Kone, Aamulehti and Vikig Line) and with operators waiting out the U.S. jobs data, which were expected to be a key factor for next week's trend.
"If the data is market friendly, there is solid demand for shares," one broker said. --Hki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 245
